comments.why_zh: 粉丝自制游戏报道深入程度的例子
comments.quote_zh: 在大多数网站上你找不到像这个一样深入的内容
comments.text_zh: 这取决于你想找哪类信息。你想了解当前中东的地缘政治局势？那基本找不到。想找类似最近那篇关于 Truecrypt 某位创始人的长篇调查报道，也一样。但如果你是 web 开发者或程序员，想找最新 JavaScript 框架之类的信息，那就能找到。你会在博客和社交网站上找到比主流新闻网站或刊物更好的信息，因为前者专注于特定主题，而后者得尽量覆盖广泛领域，深度自然就浅。至于游戏……嗯，所谓“专业”新闻一开始质量就很差。唯一会报道稍微有点意思内容的网站都是粉丝或志愿者运营的，而游戏相关媒体里最有意思的信息来源确实就是社交网站。在大多数网站上你找不到像这个一样深入的内容：[VIDEO] 即便是更普通的“新闻”类内容，通常也有大量免费、粉丝运营的替代来源。比如，没人会去主流媒体找 Pokemon 的新闻，因为他们有别的重点，而且对游戏整体了解不多。相反，他们会去众多粉丝运营网站之一，比如 Bulbanews 或 Serebii.net。大多数游戏相关的细分领域都是如此：会有几个网站直接提供信息（比主流媒体早好几个小时），然后是一大堆跟风模仿的
comments.text: Depends what kind of info you're looking for. Are you looking for information on the current middle east geopolitical situation? Then not really. Same deal if you're looking for some sort of longform investigative journalism like the recent one about one of the Truecrypt founders. But if you're a web developer or programmer looking for information about the latest Javascript frameworks or what not, then yes. You're going to find better information in blogs and on social sites that on a mainstream news site or publication, because the former cares about the specific subject and the latter has to try and cover a wide range of things to less of a degree. And in gaming... well, the 'professional' journalism is terrible quality to begin with. The only sites that cover anything remotely interesting are fan or volunteer run, and the most interesting sources for gaming related media are indeed social media sites. You're not gonna find anything as in depth at this on most sites: [VIDEO] Even for more normal 'news' stuff, there are usually tons of free and fan run alternatives. For example, no one tries to get news about Pokemon from a mainstream source, because they've got other things to focus on and don't know a lot about gaming in general. Instead, they go to one of the many fan run sites, like Bulbanews or Serebii.net. This holds true for most gaming related niches, where there'll be a few sites that provide it directly (hours ahead of the mainstream media) then a flood of copycat

comments.author: roryokane
comments.story_title: YouTube “Let's Play”s are preserving video game history
comments.why_zh: 最具文化引用度的游戏视频；解释了平行宇宙
comments.quote_zh: 不过它相当有趣，尤其是对程序员来说。
comments.text_zh: 有些 Let’s Play 我觉得比另一些更好，但我不认为其中任何一个——哪怕是最好的那些——足够流行到能成为玩家文化的一部分。不过，我认为最接近“在历史上留下印记”的游戏视频，是 pannenkoek2012 的这一个视频：[VIDEO]“SM64 - Watch for Rolling Rocks - 0.5x A Presses (Commentated)”。这是我唯一见过在完全不同的游戏视频评论区里被引用的视频。引用的是“平行宇宙”和“0.5 次 A 键按压”这些术语，而它们都在这个视频里解释过。不过，我不知道你能不能把这个视频叫作 Let’s Play，因为解说是在游戏过程之后录制的，它不是对整个游戏更大流程的一部分，而且视频里还有专门制作的动画来帮助解释游戏，而不只是原始的游戏画面。不过它相当有趣，尤其是对程序员来说。在流行的 Let’s Play 系列中，我推荐 Achievement Hunter 的 Minecraft Let’s Play 系列：[LINK]。（没错，他们抢到了“LetsPlay”这个用户名。）每一集里，Achievement Hunter 玩家团体的成员都会一起在 Minecraft 里玩一些自制活动。我不太喜欢这些玩家/解说者的个性，但挑战的创造力极其丰富，而且玩家们偶尔的搞笑表现让它值得一看。不过在 100 集之后它开始变得重复了。我再推荐几个不太知名的 Let’s Play：• Cryaotic 的 Undertale 通关流程，Pacifist
comments.text: There are Let’s Plays that I think are better than others, but I don’t think any of them, even the best of them, are popular enough to be part of gamer culture. However, the gameplay video that I think comes closest to leaving “a mark in history” is this single video by pannenkoek2012: [VIDEO] “SM64 - Watch for Rolling Rocks - 0.5x A Presses (Commentated)”. That’s the only video I’ve seen referenced in comments on videos of completely different games. The references are to “parallel universes” and “0.5 A-presses”, terms that are explained in this video. I don’t know if you could call this video a Let’s Play, though, since the commentary is recorded after the gameplay, it’s not part of a larger playthrough of the whole game, and the video has custom-made animations to aid in explaining the game, not just raw gameplay footage. It’s quite interesting, though, especially to a programmer. Among popular Let’s Play series, one I recommend is the Achievement Hunter Minecraft Let’s Play series: [LINK] . (Yup, they snagged the username “LetsPlay”.) In each episode, members of the Achievement Hunter group of players play some custom-made activity together in Minecraft. I don’t like the personalities of the players/commentators that much, but the immense creativity of the challenges and the players’ occasional funniness make it worth it. After 100 episodes it started getting repetitive though. A few other lesser-known Let’s Plays I recommend: • Cryaotic’s Undertale playthrough, Pacifist

comments.quote_zh: 那个（非常令人印象深刻的）《Watch for Rolling Rocks in 0.5 A presses》视频
comments.text_zh: 举个这类事情很重要的具体例子，还记得几年前那个（非常令人印象深刻）的《Watch for Rolling Rocks in 0.5 A presses》视频吗？[VIDEO]（给不了解的人说明一下，这个视频展示的是 Super Mario 64 的 TAS，它在通关 Watch for Rolling Rocks 关卡时，除了从进入关卡起就一直按住 A 键之外，没有再按过 A 键。）结果发现，视频中展示的路线实际上无法通过主机验证，因为他做的那些疯狂操作会在主机上触发一些恼人的 FPU 崩溃，但在模拟器上不会。不过有个好结局：在这被发现之后，有人发布了一条修正路线，它能顺利通过主机验证（前提是输入在长达 13 小时的流程中不会失同步）
comments.text: For a specific example of something like this being important, remember the (very impressive) Watch for Rolling Rocks in 0.5 A presses video from a couple years ago? [VIDEO] (For the uninitiated, this video presents a TAS of Super Mario 64 which beats the level Watch for Rolling Rocks without pressing the A button outside of keeping it held from entering the level.) It turns out that the route presented in the video actually fails console verification, since the crazy things he does trigger some annoying FPU crashes on console, but not on emulator. There is a happy end, though: a fixed route was published after this was discovered, and it passes console verification just fine (assuming the inputs dont desync over the 13 hour run)

comments.author: zamadatix

comments.text_zh: Super Mario World 的 0 exit 速通用的基本上也是完全相同的方法（包括乌龟之类的）[LINK]。SMB3 也有一个很有意思的 TAS 速通（由非人类来执行输入），在第二个手柄上快速输入会导致输入缓冲区溢出，从而让你在开始画面就能基本上瞬间通关。如果你喜欢这种因为研究如何滥用游戏而产生的有趣内容，那 The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 的历史几乎就是“然后又有人发现了更快破坏游戏的方法”。也不总是关于跑得快，挑战类速通也因大量投入而产生了许多非常有趣的结果。Super Mario 64 的 A Button Challenge（尽量用最少的 A 键次数通关）有大量极其复杂的技巧，还有精彩的讲解视频。其中一个特别引人注目，甚至成了梗[VIDEO]，尽管它其实并不是这项挑战中技术上最令人惊叹的成果。
comments.text: The 0 exit speedrun for Super Mario World uses pretty much the exact same method (koopas and all) as well [LINK] SMB3 also has an interesting tool assisted speedrun (non-human doing the inputs) where fast inputs on the second controller cause an overflow on the input buffer allowing for the game to be beaten basically instantly from the start screen. If you like this because of the interesting stuff done to abuse the game The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time has pretty much been a history of "and then a quicker way to corrupt the game was found". It's not always about going fast either, challenge runs also get a lot of very interesting results from a lot of dedication. Super Mario 64's A Button Challenge (try to beat the game with as few A presses as possible) has tons of outrageously complex tricks with amazing explanation videos. One in particular caught people's attention to the point it became a meme [VIDEO] though it's not actually the most technically impressive to come out of that endeavor.

comments.text_zh: 我能理解这为什么会让人困惑。SM64 确实区分松开前和松开后，所以严格来说游戏本身并不在意。我觉得他们想说的是，在速通中其实没有任何必要去追踪松开的时机（这一点在视频里也能得到印证：[VIDEO]）。我觉得有可能出现的情况是，如果下一关需要 0.5 次 A 键，但比如你在当前关正戴着飞行帽下落，你就得在把这半次 A 键凑成一次完整的 A 键、和戴着飞行帽下落浪费时间之间做选择。我只是觉得这不算常见情况，因为你可以走另一条路线，让按住 A 不影响你。看起来在 A Button Challenge（ABC）里，只有 5 次半按 A：[LINK]
comments.text: I could see how this could be confusing. SM64 does distinguish between before a release and after a release, so technically the game itself doesn't care. I think what they were trying to say is that there really isn't any benefit in speedrunning the game to keep track of releasing (and this can be confirmed in the video too: [VIDEO] ). I think it's possible that if the next level requires .5 a presses but, for example, you are falling with a wing cap in the current level, you have to decide between bumping that half a press into a full a press or losing time when falling with the wing cap. I just don't think it's a common case though because you could use a different route where the held A won't affect you. It looks like in the A Button Challenge (ABC), there are only 5 half a presses: [LINK]
